title: Extra, Extra
summary: A newsboy at the docks, a historian at the library, and a door that is not supposed to exist.

steps.name: Danny
lines: Eli! You hear the radio? Austria’s gone. Just like that. My pop says it’s 1914 all over again, only this time the planes will come.
Listen, there’s a professor lady at the Old Town library paying two bits for anybody who’s seen the Bureau sealing up doors. You’ve seen one. Down at the bridge. Go tell her.
steps.objective: Talk to Danny the newsboy at the Docks

steps.name: Professor Ada Varga
lines: You saw them seal it? Under the Meridian Bridge? Then you saw more than the Bureau wants anyone to see.
They are called chronoports. Rings of stone older than the city. Each one opens on a single year, and the Bureau has made it a crime to use them. The Act of 1921.
My notes say the bridge door opens on Rome, the year Trajan finished his forum. I cannot go. They watch me. You, they do not know yet.
The seal is only a padlock on a gate the Bureau does not understand. Go to the west pier at low water. Come back and tell me what Rome looks like the year it stopped growing.
steps.objective: Find Professor Varga at the Old Town library
Go to the west pier of the Meridian Bridge
steps.label: Meridian Bridge

steps.objective: Find the sealed chronoport
Step through the chronoport (press E at the ring)

completeText: The ring is warm. The bridge is gone. The year is 112.

title: Bread and Circuses
summary: Rome at its largest. Find out what holds a city of a million together, and what it costs.

steps.name: Fortunata
lines: A stranger in strange clothes, asking how Rome works. Simple. The emperor gives us bread, water and games, and we give him quiet.
Two hundred thousand families on the grain dole. The grain comes from Egypt on ships. If the ships stop, the quiet stops.
You want to know what holds it together? Go up to the Capitol and ask a senator. They own the ships.
steps.objective: Ask around in the Forum

steps.name: Pliny
lines: The dole? The dole is cheap. Dacia paid for it. The next war will pay for the next dole. There is always a next war.
You ask what happens when there is no next war. A good question. Nobody who asks it keeps his seat in the Senate.
Go to the Emporium. The harbor master keeps the ledger of every grain ship. Read it, and you will understand Rome better than most emperors.
steps.objective: Climb to the Capitol and speak with Senator Pliny

steps.name: Grain ledger
lines: The ledger lists 1,200 ships a year from Alexandria. A note in the margin: "Short by 90 this year. Egypt floods late. Raise the frontier levy."
Every problem in this city is solved by taking something from somewhere further away. The map on the wall shows how far away is left: not far.
steps.objective: Read the grain ledger at the Emporium
Return to 1938 through the chronoport

steps.name: Professor Ada Varga
lines: Overextension. A city that could only stand by growing. Write it down. Every lesson you bring back, write it down.
I have found two more doors. One is under this very building, in the philosophy stacks. The other is at the old North Station. The Bureau has not reached either.
Go. Learn how the old ones ended. All of them, if you can. Somebody has to, before we find out the hard way.
steps.objective: Report to Professor Varga

title: Hale’s Ledger
summary: The factories on the Eastside are humming again. Find out what they are making.

steps.name: Walt
lines: Hale Armaments. Three shifts. We make shell casings and we do not ask who they are for. The pay is good. The pay is very good.
Hale has Bureau men at the gate. Why does a shell plant need the Bureau of Temporal Compliance? You tell me, kid.
Word is Hale bought the rights to every sealed door in the city. Bought them. From the government. For a dollar each.
steps.objective: Talk to Walt outside the Hale plant on the Eastside

steps.name: Cornelius Hale
lines: Mr. Marsh. The professor’s errand boy. I know about the bridge. I know about Rome. I have people in Rome.
You think the doors are a lesson. They are a market. A man who knows the price of grain in every century never loses a trade. A man who knows which wars happen never loses a war.
Keep walking through doors if you like. Every time you do, you tell me which ones work. Good day.
steps.objective: Confront Cornelius Hale on the steps of City Hall

completeText: Hale is using you to map the doors. You will need to find the rest before he does.

title: The Pattern
summary: You have seen enough civilizations fall to see the shape of it. Time to say so out loud.

steps.name: Professor Ada Varga
lines: Eight lessons. Salt in the soil, a river that forgot, one bad day, a web that broke. Fear as a loan, divided cities, an empire of one man, a frontier that was a countdown.
None of them fell to an enemy they could not have beaten. They fell to a problem they had decided not to look at.
Hale wants the doors to make money from the war that is coming. The Bureau wants them sealed so nobody has to think about it. You and I want them open so everybody does.
Write it all down. Put it in the paper. Danny will sell it for two cents. That is how civilizations learn: late, and in print.
steps.objective: Meet Professor Varga at the war memorial

steps.name: Danny
lines: A story about doors in time and every empire that ever fell? Mister, nobody is going to believe a word of it.
Extra! Extra! Read all about it! Two cents! ...They’re buying it, Eli. They’re actually buying it.
steps.objective: Give the story to Danny at the Docks

completeText: The story is out. The doors are still open. What you do with the rest of history is up to you.

title: The Divided City
summary: Athens and Thebes have finally allied. Philip is already marching.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 338 BCE (the back stacks of the Old Town public library)
Travel to The Polis, 338 BCE

steps.name: Demosthenes
lines: Ten years I told them Philip was coming. They laughed, then they voted me the theatre budget to shut me up.
Now Thebes is with us. Now. A month before the battle. Go up to the Acropolis and ask the generals how long they have trained together.
steps.objective: Talk to Demosthenes at the The Agora Quarter plaza

steps.name: Phocion
lines: Two armies that hated each other a year ago, standing in one line. The line will hold until it does not.
Chaeronea. Next week. Philip’s son is eighteen and commands the cavalry. His name is Alexander. Remember it.
The oracle at the sacred grove has the decree of the alliance carved in stone. Read how long it took to agree.
steps.objective: Climb to the Acropolis and speak with Phocion

steps.name: Decree of Alliance
lines: "Resolved, in the archonship of Chaerondas, that Athens and Thebes make common cause." The date is this spring. The quarrel it ends began before the signers were born.
A hundred years of free cities, united for one month, by a man they could have stopped ten years ago.
steps.objective: Read the Decree of Alliance at the Academy Groves sacred ground

title: Smoke and Glass
summary: The Great Exhibition has opened a glass palace to the world. The city around it cannot breathe.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1851 CE (the bricked-up platform of the abandoned North Station)
Travel to The Crystal City, 1851 CE

steps.name: Nell
lines: Fourteen hours, six days, and the engine does not stop so neither do we. My sister is ten. She works the looms.
The gentlemen are up at Parliament Hill deciding whether children under nine should be in the mills. Under nine! Ask them how they decided that number.
steps.objective: Talk to Nell at the The City plaza

steps.name: Mr. Paxton
lines: A million panes of glass. The future, on display for a shilling. We can build anything. We have simply not decided what to build.
The sewers? The sewers are a question for the next Parliament. The cholera is a question for the next summer.
There is a notice at the cathedral about the water. A doctor named Snow. Nobody is reading it. You should.
steps.objective: Climb to the Parliament Hill and speak with Mr. Paxton

steps.name: Dr. Snow’s Notice
lines: "The cholera clusters about the Broad Street pump. Remove the handle." Someone has written underneath: "Removed. Deaths stopped. Handle replaced by order of the parish."
They knew. They had the answer in a single sentence. They put the handle back because the alternative was admitting the city had outgrown their idea of it.
steps.objective: Read the Dr. Snow’s Notice at the Railway Town sacred ground

title: The Salt in the Soil
summary: The first city on Earth, and the first city to run out of soil.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 3200 BCE (the collapsed cistern behind the West Market rail yard)
Travel to Uruk of the Reeds, 3200 BCE

steps.name: Geme
lines: Wheat used to grow here. Now barley. Soon, not barley. The white crust comes up with the water and stays when the water goes.
The temple says pray. The temple owns the fields, so the temple can say what it likes. Go up to the Eanna precinct and ask a priest why they do not let the fields rest.
steps.objective: Talk to Geme at the Old Reed Quarter plaza

steps.name: Enheduanna
lines: Let the fields rest? The city eats every year. The soldiers eat every year. The gods, I assure you, eat every year.
We dig new canals further out. The salt follows. We dig further. There is a tablet at the standing stones with the harvest counts for forty years. Read it, if you can bear to.
steps.objective: Climb to the Eanna Precinct and speak with Enheduanna

steps.name: Harvest Tablet
lines: Forty years of harvests, pressed in clay. The wheat column ends twenty years ago. The barley column has been shrinking for ten.
Somebody counted all of this, carefully, every year, and nobody changed anything. Counting is not the same as deciding.
steps.objective: Read the Harvest Tablet at the Gate of Inanna sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: The Salt in the Soil.

title: When the River Forgot
summary: The Great Pyramid is finished. The god-king guarantees the flood. The nilometer disagrees.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 2560 BCE (the sealed vault under the Northgate cemetery chapel)
Travel to Men-nefer on the River, 2560 BCE

steps.name: Merer
lines: Ten loaves, two jugs of beer, and a pyramid for a god who promises the river will rise. It has risen every year of my life. Why would it stop?
The priests at the Horizon measure the river. Ask them what they measured this year. Ask them twice; they lie the first time.
steps.objective: Talk to Merer at the White Walls plaza

steps.name: Hemiunu
lines: The nilometer reads low. Three years low. The granaries are full because we built them for the flood years. For how long? Do not ask that question in front of Pharaoh.
He is a god. The flood is his promise. When a god’s promise fails, the god does not fall. The order that believed him does. The sphinx has the old flood marks carved on its base. Read them.
steps.objective: Climb to the Horizon of Khufu and speak with Hemiunu

steps.name: Flood Marks
lines: Forty flood marks, one per year, carved into the stone. The last three are below all the others. Below them, a newer, smaller mark that someone has tried to scratch out.
A state built on one promise is a state with one point of failure. The river is not listening to the Pharaoh. It never was.
steps.objective: Read the Flood Marks at the The Necropolis Road sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: When the River Forgot.

title: One Bad Day
summary: A sea empire with no walls, fleets on every horizon and ash falling on the orchards.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1600 BCE (the flooded boathouse at the east end of the Old Harbor)
Travel to Knossos by the Sea, 1600 BCE

steps.name: Kydon
lines: No walls! Why walls? We own every ship on the sea. Who would attack an island that owns the sea?

The mountain on Thera has been smoking for a month. The priestesses say the earth-bull is restless. The sailors say the water near Thera is warm. Go to the Labyrinth and ask the priestess what the bull wants.
steps.objective: Talk to Kydon at the The Lower Town plaza

steps.name: Pasiphae
lines: The bull wants what it always wants. Blood, saffron, dancers. We give it, and the sea stays calm. The sea has been calm for three hundred years.
Ash on the orchards this morning. The children thought it was snow. The peak sanctuary has the old offering records. Go and read how long since the mountain last spoke.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Labyrinth and speak with Pasiphae

steps.name: Offering Record
lines: Three hundred years of offerings. Not one mention of the mountain. Not one plan for the fleet being gone. Not one wall.
Everything here depends on the sea staying what it has always been. It will not, and there is no second plan, because a second plan would admit the first one could fail.
steps.objective: Read the Offering Record at the Cypress Terraces sacred ground

title: The Web Breaks
summary: Palace kingdoms linked by bronze, counted on clay, and about to go dark together.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1250 BCE (the cave behind the reservoir on the back slope of Citadel Hill)
Travel to The Lion Citadel, 1250 BCE

steps.name: Eumaios
lines: Two bad harvests, and the palace still takes its share, and the gods still take theirs. The hills are filling up with men who used to be farmers.
The bronze comes from an island so far west the sun sets on it. The tin comes from further. Go up to the Lion Gate and ask the scribe what happens if one ship does not come.
steps.objective: Talk to Eumaios at the Lower Town plaza

steps.name: Alxoitas
lines: Every jar of oil, every chariot wheel, every slave, on a tablet in the palace. If one ship does not come, we read the tablets and reassign. If ten ships do not come...
The wanax has called for ships for a war across the sea. Over a woman, they say. Over the tin routes, I say. The grave circle has the tablet of the Sea Peoples. Read it, and then forget you did.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Lion Gate and speak with Alxoitas

steps.name: Tablet of the Sea Peoples
lines: "Raiders from the sea. Pylos burned. Send chariots." The tablet was baked hard in a fire. The fire was the palace.
Every palace depended on every other palace. When the ships stopped, the bronze stopped, the writing stopped, and for four hundred years nobody could read this.
steps.objective: Read the Tablet of the Sea Peoples at the Tomb Road sacred ground

title: Fear Is a Loan
summary: The most feared army on Earth throws a ten-day feast. Its guests are counting the days.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 879 BCE (the abandoned gatehouse on the east ring road)
Travel to Kalhu of the Winged Bulls, 879 BCE

steps.name: Hoshea
lines: They marched us a thousand miles to build a palace for a king we had never heard of. We will not forget where we came from. None of us will.
Seventy thousand guests at the feast. The king will carve it on the wall. Go up to the palace and ask a courtier who does the carving.
steps.objective: Talk to Hoshea at the Lower City plaza

steps.name: Bel-tarsi
lines: The king flays rebels and nails the skins to the wall. The next city opens its gates without a fight. Efficient, yes? Ask me who guards the wall at night. Deportees.

Every province sends tribute. Every province hates us. One is the cause of the other, and the king knows it, and the king does not care. The stele at the small ziggurat lists the provinces. Count them.
steps.objective: Climb to the The North-West Palace and speak with Bel-tarsi

steps.name: Tribute Stele
lines: Forty-one provinces, each with the tribute owed and the punishment for shortfall. The punishments get longer toward the bottom of the list.
Terror works until the day everyone it works on decides to stop being afraid at the same time. The stele is a list of everyone who will be at Nineveh when it burns.
steps.objective: Read the Tribute Stele at the Gate of Nergal sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: Fear Is a Loan.

title: The Empire of One Man
summary: A conqueror became a pacifist and carved the rules on pillars. The rules depend on the man.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 250 BCE (the overgrown bandstand in West Ring Park)
Travel to Pataliputra of the Pillars, 250 BCE

steps.name: Upagupta
lines: The emperor killed a hundred thousand at Kalinga, wept, and wrote the rules on stone. All beings wish to live. Also, the tax rate.
Dhamma is not a religion. It is a way of not needing an army. Go to the pillared hall and ask an official whether the army agrees.
steps.objective: Talk to Upagupta at the Old Pataliputra plaza

steps.name: Radhagupta
lines: The Arthashastra has several chapters on spies. We are very well informed. We know, for instance, that the princes do not share their father’s opinion on war.
An empire this size holds together by the will of one man. Think about what that means for the second man. The great stupa has the succession edict. Read who is named.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Pillared Hall and speak with Radhagupta

steps.name: Succession Edict
lines: The edict names no heir. It names Dhamma as the heir. A law cannot command an elephant.
Fifty years from now this empire will be in pieces, because its genius was a person and not a system. The pillars will outlast the empire by two thousand years.
steps.objective: Read the Succession Edict at the Monastery Road sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: The Empire of One Man.

title: The Forest Does Not Return
summary: A jungle city of astronomers, on the day strangers arrive and the king dies.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 378 CE (the sinkhole in the vacant lot at the south-west corner of the ring road)
Travel to Mutal of the Jungle, 378 CE

steps.name: Balam
lines: Burn the forest, plant the maize, move on. The forest used to come back in seven years. Now it takes twenty. The city grows and the forest shrinks. Somebody should do the arithmetic.
The astronomers can tell you the day of an eclipse a thousand years out. Go up to the acropolis and ask them what day the rains come.
steps.objective: Talk to Balam at the Plaza of the Stelae plaza

steps.name: Chak Tok
lines: Venus returns every 584 days. We are correct to the day. The rains are less reliable than Venus. The king is less reliable than the rains.
The strangers from the west arrived today. The king entered the water today. We are writing it down very carefully. The observatory keeps the reservoir counts. Look at them.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Great Acropolis and speak with Chak Tok

steps.name: Reservoir Count
lines: Rainfall, by year, scratched into the observatory wall. The dry years come in pairs now, then threes. The reservoirs were built for one.
They planned for the worst drought they had ever seen. They had not seen the worst drought. Plan for the record and then assume the record will be broken.
steps.objective: Read the Reservoir Count at the The Observatory Road sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: The Forest Does Not Return.

title: Short Summers
summary: Raiders became settlers overnight. Nobody has told the winters.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 866 CE (the derelict ferry slip south of the harbor)
Travel to Jorvik of the Long Ships, 866 CE

steps.name: Astrid
lines: Every family gets its own plot. Every family needs its own plot. We do not share well. Ask my neighbor. Ask his axe.
The old men say the winters are getting shorter and that is the gods being kind. Go to the jarl’s hall and ask the skald what the gods do when they change their minds.
steps.objective: Talk to Astrid at the The Old Burh plaza

steps.name: Egil
lines: Ragnarok. The gods lose, the world ends, and a new one grows. We tell the children this so they are not afraid of endings. We should tell it to the farmers.
The settlers in the west build the same farms they built at home, on land that is not home. They will not eat fish. The sea is full of fish. The runestone at the hof says why. Read it.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Jarl’s Hall and speak with Egil

steps.name: The Hof Runestone
lines: "Thorvald raised this stone for his father, who kept the old ways in the new land." Below it, smaller: "and starved."
They had every tool they needed to adapt, except the willingness. Adaptation is not weakness; it is the only thing that ever survived a changing climate.
steps.objective: Read the The Hof Runestone at the The Thing Fields sacred ground

title: The Machine Needs Tending
summary: The largest city on Earth runs on water. The engineers are losing to the silt.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1150 CE (the pump house in the east-bank water works)
Travel to Angkor of the Waters, 1150 CE

steps.name: Sok
lines: Two harvests a year, three if the canals are good. The canals are the king’s. So the harvest is the king’s. My grandfather dug canals. My father dug canals. I dig canals.
The forest is cut for the temples. When the rains come, the hills come down with them. Go to the temple mountain and ask an engineer how much silt a god weighs.
steps.objective: Talk to Sok at the The Royal Enclosure plaza

steps.name: Kambu
lines: The barays hold a year of rain. The canals move it to the rice, the rice to the king. One machine. Beautiful. Every year a little more silt, and we dredge, and we are always dredging.
The new king wants a bigger temple. The temple needs stone. The stone needs the forest. The forest held the hills. The naga bridge has the water marks. Read them.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Temple Mountain and speak with Kambu

steps.name: Water Marks
lines: Flood heights, carved into the naga balustrade. They rise for a century. Then, two years ago, a flood so high it tore out the main channel. This year, nothing came at all.
Infrastructure is a promise to the future that the future has to keep paying for. Angkor stopped paying, and the water went where it liked.
steps.objective: Read the Water Marks at the The Northern Canals sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: The Machine Needs Tending.

title: Inherited Like a Herd
summary: The horde crushed Europe’s knights and stopped. The Great Khan is dead.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1241 CE (the stone cairn on the hill beyond the north-west ring road)
Travel to The Ordu on the Plain, 1241 CE

steps.name: Subutai
lines: Five horses per man. We ride one, eat one, and the others carry what we took. The knights of Hungary charged us at Mohi. We let them. Then we closed the circle.
The Khan is dead. Every prince must ride home to choose the next one. So Europe lives. Go to the golden ordu and ask the envoy who chooses.
steps.objective: Talk to Subutai at the Captives’ Camp plaza

steps.name: Carpini
lines: A letter travels from here to Karakorum in two weeks. Nothing in Christendom moves that fast except rumor. And yet the empire stops dead because one man died and there is no rule for the next.
Four grandsons, four khanates. Watch what happens to an empire inherited like a herd. The ovoo cairn has the stones of every prince who has already left. Count them.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Golden Ordu and speak with Carpini

steps.name: The Ovoo
lines: A cairn of stones, one for each prince riding home to vote. More stones than there are votes. Some of these princes will not come back from the choosing.
The largest empire in history, and no procedure for the morning after. A system with no rule for passing power has its civil war already scheduled.
steps.objective: Read the The Ovoo at the The Scouts’ Line sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: Inherited Like a Herd.

title: Allies of the Enemy
summary: A floating capital fed by two hundred cities that hate it. Strangers with horses have landed.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1519 CE (the drained ornamental pond in Riverside Gardens)
Travel to Tenochtitlan of the Lake, 1519 CE

steps.name: Xochitl
lines: Seven harvests a year on the floating gardens. A thousand canoes bring food every morning. Cut the causeways and the city starves in a week. Everyone knows this. Including the Tlaxcalans.
Men on the coast with deer the size of houses. The emperor sent them gold. Go to the sacred precinct and ask an eagle warrior what he would have sent.
steps.objective: Talk to Xochitl at the Teopan plaza

steps.name: Cuauhtemoc
lines: We do not conquer to kill. We conquer to collect. Every city pays, every city hates us, every city waits. The strangers have found something better than horses: people who hate us.
A One Reed year. The year the feathered serpent was promised to return. The sun stone has the omens of this year carved on it. Count them.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Sacred Precinct and speak with Cuauhtemoc

steps.name: The Sun Stone
lines: A comet. A temple that burned without fire. A woman weeping in the streets at night. A bird with a mirror in its head. Eight omens in one year, all carved before the ships came.
Five hundred Spaniards did not take this city. Tens of thousands of people who had been paying tribute for a century did. An empire built on resentment hands its enemies an army.
steps.objective: Read the The Sun Stone at the Cuepopan sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: Allies of the Enemy.

title: The Peace After the War
summary: The armies gather at Sekigahara. One battle ends a century of war, and everything the war made possible.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1600 CE (the walled garden behind the Eastside tea house)
Travel to Castle Town of the Divided Realm, 1600 CE

steps.name: Yodoya
lines: Merchants are the lowest class. We also own everything. Whoever wins tomorrow will owe money to someone on this street.
The sword hunt took every blade from the villages. Now only samurai have swords, and only samurai have a say. Go up to the castle and ask a samurai what peace will look like.
steps.objective: Talk to Yodoya at the Samurai Quarter plaza

steps.name: Tadakatsu
lines: A hundred years of every lord against every lord. Tomorrow, one battle ends it. Then Ieyasu will make peace boring: disarm everyone, freeze every class, close every port.
Two hundred years without war, bought with everything the war made possible. The arquebus. The trade. The questions. The pagoda has the edict already drafted. Read it.
steps.objective: Climb to the The Honmaru and speak with Tadakatsu

steps.name: The Draft Edict
lines: "No ship shall leave. No foreigner shall land. No peasant shall bear arms. No man shall change his station." The ink is not dry. The battle has not been fought.
Stability has a price too. They will pay it for two and a half centuries and call it peace, and when the black ships come they will have forgotten how to do anything else.
steps.objective: Read the The Draft Edict at the The Rice Stores sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: The Peace After the War.

title: Pardoned Out of Existence
summary: The pirate republic has a vote and a constitution. The governor has a pardon and four warships.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1718 CE (the smugglers’ cove below the south-west sea wall)
Travel to Port Royal of the Black Flag, 1718 CE

steps.name: Caesar
lines: Freer on a pirate ship than anywhere else in this ocean, and that is a low bar. One vote per man, equal shares, captain only gives orders in a fight.
The king offers a pardon to any pirate who quits. Half of Nassau took it. Go to the fort and ask the governor’s man why the other half is still drinking.
steps.objective: Talk to Caesar at the Thames Street plaza

steps.name: Hornigold
lines: I took the pardon. I hunt my old crewmates now for the Crown. Why? Because honesty got cheaper than theft the day the navy showed up. That is the whole story of piracy.
Teach is blockading Charleston this week for a chest of medicine. Theatre. Theatre works until it does not. The lighthouse keeper logs every ship that takes the pardon. Go count.
steps.objective: Climb to the Fort Charles and speak with Hornigold

steps.name: Lighthouse Log
lines: Ships in: forty-one. Pardons taken: thirty-three. Beneath the numbers, a note in a different hand: "Rogers arrives with the fleet in July. Make it forty."
The republic was not defeated. It was dissolved by paperwork and a better offer. Movements built on grievance evaporate the moment the grievance is cheaper to settle than to fight.
steps.objective: Read the Lighthouse Log at the The Plantations sacred ground

completeText: Insight gained: Pardoned Out of Existence.

title: The Frontier Closes
summary: Gold in the hills, a railroad coming, and news from Little Bighorn a week old.

steps.objective: Find the chronoport to 1876 CE (the dry well in the old livery yard off Kings Road)
Travel to Deadwood on the Line, 1876 CE

steps.name: Calamity
lines: The railroad gets here next year. Then the cattle drives end and so does every job I know how to do. The buffalo are gone. Sixty million, gone in twenty years. We did that on purpose.
This is Lakota land by treaty. The treaty lasted until somebody found gold. Go up to the fort and ask the colonel what a treaty is for.
steps.objective: Talk to Calamity at the Main Street plaza

steps.name: Colonel
lines: A treaty is for the time it takes to find a reason to break it. Custer took two hundred men against two thousand because he thought the frontier was still endless. News travels slow. Lessons travel slower.
The frontier is not a resource. It is a countdown. The church has the land office map. Look how much is left.
steps.objective: Climb to the Fort Hill and speak with Colonel

steps.name: Land Office Map
lines: A map of the territory with the claims colored in. Twenty years ago the map was white. Now there is one white patch, and a railroad drawn through the middle of it in pencil.
The West was sold as endless. It took one generation to fence it, mine it and lay a track across it. Every frontier ends; the only question is whether you planned for the ending.
steps.objective: Read the Land Office Map at the The Badlands Road sacred ground
